title: Benzotriazolium picrate
authors: Zeng B, Li J, Wang G
journal: Acta Crystallographica Section E Structure Reports Online
claims: An independent room-temperature determination of benzotriazolium picrate (C6H6N3+ C6H2N3O7-) found a second monoclinic form, P21/n with a = 14.411, b = 3.761, c = 24.941 A and Z = 4, in which both N-H groups of the doubly N-protonated cation (N4-H4...O1 2.799 A, N6-H6...O1 2.770 A) donate to the phenolate oxygen, building chains along [010] supported by C-H...O contacts and pi-pi stacking with a 3.908 A centroid-centroid distance.

title: A theoretical study of the parent NH-benzazoles (benzimidazoles, indazoles and benzotriazoles): geometries, energies, acidity and basicity, NMR properties and molecular electrostatic potentials
authors: Alkorta I, Sï¿½nchez-Sanz G, Trujillo C et al.
claims: At the same B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) level used here, the parent NH-benzazoles including benzotriazole were optimised and compared with X-ray geometries, tautomer energies, measured pKa values, NMR shifts and molecular electrostatic potentials, giving a benchmark for the neutral benzotriazole framework from which the cation is derived.

EDITOR CORRECTION (round 1, full text read: open-access Arkivoc PDF): besides neutral 1H-benzotriazole (12), the study optimises the 1,3-diH benzotriazolium cation (14) = 1H-benzotriazol-3-ium, the BTPC cation, at B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) and compares it with averaged CSD X-ray structures (Table 1): N-N 1.309 calc / 1.312 X-ray; angle 2-3-3a at the protonated N 113.4 / 112.6 deg; neutral 12, angle 2-3-3a at the unprotonated N3 108.7 / 108.2 deg. Protonation of benzotriazole gives the 1,3-diH cation, the only one found in crystals (p. 5, p. 8). Basicity pKa of benzotriazole 1.6 quoted from the authors' compilation of azole acid-base data (p. 8).

title: Photochemistry of 1H-Benzotriazole in Aqueous Solution: A Photolatent Base
authors: Wang H, Burda C, Persy G et al.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
claims: Flash-photolysis work on 1H-benzotriazole corrected the acidity constant of the N-protonated benzotriazolium cation to pKa = 0.42 +/- 0.02 (I = 1.0 M), so benzotriazole is a very weak base whose cation is only formed in strongly acidic water.

title: Is It Salt, Cocrystal, or Continuum? Successes and Limitations of Computationally Efficient Periodic System Calculations
